To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) tensor-based composition outperforms vector-based composition in terms of the entailment degrees, and (ii) the holistic method is the most successful in terms of the overall entailment degree, and the relational and Frobenius methods are the best in terms of the word-based entailment measures.
(1) the holistic method performs best on all three datasets, (2) the best measure is the APinc measure, and (3) the best combination of the two is APinc+holistic.
(i) the Frobenius model is the only one that outperforms vector-based composition on all three datasets; and that (ii) the best performing measure for the Frobenius tensor-based composition is APinc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can the distributional inclusion property be extended to the tensor-based setting?
the theoretical and empirical analysis of entailment between words and their compositions.
the question of how well the distributional inclusion principle can be extended from the word to the sentence level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best method of tensor composition, but that the best model depends on the dataset and on which measure is being used.
the holistic model is a promising choice, especially when the entailment is measured with APinc, bal-APinc, or our previously proposed measures.
the holistic model is the best one, and that the tensor-based approach is better than the simple vector-based one, but not by much, especially for the APinc and balAPinc measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for all three entailment datasets and all three sentence-level measures, the relational method achieves the highest accuracy.
holistic composition is the best choice in terms of the sentence-level measures, whereas the projective method performs better in combination with word-based measures.
the Frobenius model, with the exception of the KL-divergence metric, outperforms all other methods in all datasets and measures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the holistic model outperforms other models on all three datasets and all measures.
the holistic model is superior to other methods, and that the best results can be obtained when using the holistic model in combination with our previously proposed sentence-level measures.
the tensor models are not always better than the simple vector models, and that the choice of tensor composition method is important.
